title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
statement: `heights[r][c]` is the height of each cell of an island. The **Pacific** touches the top and left edges, the **Atlantic** the bottom and right edges. Rain water flows from a cell to a neighbour that is **equal or lower**. Return all cells from which water can reach **both** oceans.

example.why: The two corners touch both oceans directly, and the peak (5) drains up or left into the Pacific and down or right into the Atlantic.

idea: Testing every cell with its own search (*can I flow down to each ocean?*) repeats a huge amount of work.
Turn it around: start **at the ocean** and walk **uphill** (to neighbours that are equal or higher). Every cell reached this way can send water back down the same path into that ocean.
Do this once from all Pacific border cells and once from all Atlantic border cells. The answer is the cells reached by **both** walks.

complexity.timeWhy: Each cell is visited at most once per ocean.
complexity.spaceWhy: Two sets of cells plus the recursion stack.

steps.text: Our example: **`heights = [[4,2,3],[1,5,2],[3,1,1]]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
